title: Binary tree zigzag level order
label: idb-list
statement: Return the values of a binary tree **level by level**, reading the first level left to right, the next right to left, and alternating from there.
provenance: **InterviewDB-listed.** LeetCode 103 is on the LinkedIn list you supplied from InterviewDB. No candidate report of this exact question was found in the research passes — the evidence is that the list names it. On that list it uses the same pattern as InterviewDB Q10. Level-by-level processing, measured from the root. Q10’s levels are measured from the leaves, which is why BFS does not work for it and a post-order pass does. Doing both back to back is the cleanest way to feel that difference.

stages.title: Zigzag levels

stages.require: Implement `Zigzag.Levels(root)`: level 0 left-to-right, level 1 right-to-left, and so on. Empty tree → empty list.

1.a: Ask; this one starts left to right.

2.a: A deque: add to the front or back depending on the level. Same cost.

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Return the values of a binary tree **level by level**, reading the first level left to right, the next right to left, and alternating from there.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Direction of the first level? (Left to right.)
- Empty tree? (Empty list.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: It is ordinary breadth-first search by level. Take exactly `queue.Count` nodes for each level, and reverse every other level's list. Changing the order you *enqueue* children is where people tie themselves in knots — reversing the finished level is simpler.

learn.title: 4 · Approach

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Alternating the order of enqueuing children — that corrupts the next level.
- Not snapshotting the level size before the loop, so levels blur together.
- Inserting at the front of a List for odd levels (O(width) per insert).
